title: Garden and Veil Anew
premise: Emrys Ashgrove, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Greyhollow, watches the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night—signs that the Veil between realms is dying and the long winter will swallow both worlds. Hunted by the Warden's inquisitors and guided by a found family of smugglers, hedge-witches, and one very stubborn cartographer, Emrys must journey to the ruined Covenant Stones where their mother once bound the realms together. There they learn the covenant was never broken by accident: it was deliberately sundered by the Wardens' founder, who stole its memory-threads to build his power. In the climax, Emrys reforges the covenant not with blood or obedience but with freely given memory, sacrificing their own recollection of exile to reignite the stars—and chooses to stay, no longer invisible, among the people who became their home.
about_author: Juniper Joubert is the pen name of a former botanist who traded field notebooks for fantasy manuscripts after a decade cataloguing alpine wildflowers. They write stories about stubborn people, small magics, and the families we build when the old ones fail us.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Selling charms in Greyhollow's night market, Emrys feels the wards shatter and watches every star extinguish at once. The emotional beat is dread masked by routine—the moment invisibility stops being a choice.

chapters.title: Charms for a Dying City
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Next morning, panic ripples through Greyhollow; Emrys quietly heals a frostbitten child, breaking their own rules. Beat: compassion reawakening after twenty years of self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Sable Vane, a sharp-tongued mapmaker, confronts Emrys, having traced the ward-failure to the old Covenant Stones. Beat: reluctant alliance; Sable sees through Emrys's disguise instantly.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Inquisitors raid the market quarter hunting 'residual casters.' Emrys hides their storm-glass amulet and nearly burns a neighbor. Beat: guilt and the cost of staying hidden.

chapters.title: The Lamplighter's Daughter
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip, a teenage lamplighter and secret hedge-witch, begs Emrys to teach her before the winter takes her sick mother. Beat: Emrys refusing, then relenting—found family begins.

chapters.title: What the Frost Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Frost patterns spell out Emrys's childhood name—a message from the dying Veil itself. Beat: uncanny grief; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Smugglers of the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The crew meets the Bramble twins, smugglers who can move them past the checkpoints toward the Stones. Beat: wary camaraderie, humor against fear.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, flashback-heavy. How Emrys was exiled after a storm they called killed three people—including, they believe, their brother. Beat: shame as the story's engine revealed.

chapters.title: The Warden's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. High Warden Corvess announces curfews and mandatory 'purity attestations,' blaming magic-users for the darkened sky. Beat: rising oppression; Pip's defiance kindles.

chapters.title: Crossing the Ashline
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The group slips through the burned borderlands where the wards fell, finding the land drained of color. Beat: awe and horror at the Veil's wound made visible.

chapters.title: The Inn at Lastlight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Shelter at an inn run by Marrow, an ex-Warden deserter who recognizes Emrys. Beat: tension, then unexpected kindness—Marrows feeds them and asks nothing.

chapters.title: Storm-Glass
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys's amulet cracks; each use now costs memories. They practice small callings with Pip, losing the taste of their mother's bread. Beat: sacrifice has a price, foreshadowing the ending.

chapters.title: Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. A village en route has gone silent, its people standing frozen mid-task, memory-drained. Beat: dread; the long winter eats minds first.

chapters.title: The Founder's Lie
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In a ruined archive, Sable deciphers records: Warden founder Aldric Veyra sundered the covenant himself, weaving stolen realm-memories into his bloodline. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Corvess Hunts
chapters.summary: Corvess's POV. The High Warden, secretly Veyra's heir, needs a covenant-heir's blood to renew her stolen power. She closes on Emrys's trail. Beat: antagonist given weight and motive.

chapters.title: What My Brother Saw
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Marrow reveals the truth of the exile-storm: Emrys's brother Tam survived and testified falsely under Warden pressure. Beat: grief inverted—shame built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Brambles Stand
chapters.summary: Bramble twin POV (shared). A checkpoint ambush; the twins hold the pass so the others escape, one gravely wounded. Beat: found family bleeding for each other.

chapters.title: Snowbound Confessions
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Trapped in a cave, Emrys tells Pip and Sable the whole story of the storm and Tam. Beat: vulnerability as turning point; the mask comes off for good.

chapters.title: Pip's First Storm
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip calls her first lightning to save them from wolves, terrified and triumphant. Beat: inheritance passed on; mentorship becomes partnership.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They pass through Veyra's abandoned capital, where citizens wander memoryless among grand monuments to stolen glory. Beat: thematic core—the cost of hoarded memory.

chapters.title: Corvess Offers a Bargain
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Corvess corners them: help her reforge the covenant under Warden control and Tam lives; refuse and he dies. Beat: impossible choice; Emrys stalls, heartbroken.

chapters.title: Tam Ashgrove
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Revealed alive and serving as Corvess's warden-captain, Tam wrestles with his false testimony and his sister's return. Beat: antagonist's blade is also family.

chapters.title: The Road to the Stones
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Final ascent through ever-deepening winter; supplies fail; Sable maps a path no one else could. Beat: quiet resolve; the found family holds.

chapters.title: Veil-Sickness
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip begins forgetting—her mother's face first—as the Veil's decay spreads. Beat: urgency sharpened into personal stakes.

chapters.title: The Covenant Stones
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They reach the shattered Stones and read the original covenant: memory freely given, realm to realm. Beat: understanding what must be done—and what it costs.

chapters.title: Aldric's Echo
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Within the Stones, Aldric Veyra's preserved echo tests them with illusions of their deepest wants. Beat: temptation resisted; Sable rejects a vision of her lost home.

chapters.title: Corvess Descends
chapters.summary: Corvess's POV. The High Warden arrives with an army and Tam, demanding the Stones. Beat: all threads converge; armies ring the mountain.

chapters.title: Brother Against Winter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys and Tam face each other; Emrys refuses to fight, offering instead the truth of that night. Beat: love disarming violence; Tam falters.

chapters.title: The Stolen Threads
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inside the covenant lattice, they find generations of stolen memories woven into Corvess's claim. Beat: horror at the machinery of inherited power.

chapters.title: Pip Gives Her Light
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip offers her own bright memories willingly to start the reforging, buying time. Beat: the youngest teaches everyone what free giving means.

chapters.title: Corvess Unraveled
chapters.summary: Corvess's POV. Offered her ancestors' true memories back, Corvess takes them—and the theft unmakes her certainty, then her power. Beat: villain defeated by truth, not force.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Climax: Emrys gives up their memories of exile—twenty years of loneliness—to bind the covenant anew. Beat: transcendence through sacrifice; the stars relight one by one.

chapters.title: After the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, remembering everything now, kneels in the snow asking nothing; Emrys, memory-light, greets him as a stranger might—with open curiosity. Beat: bittersweet grace.

chapters.title: Stars Over Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The company returns to a city waking under stars, magic no longer outlawed but unregulated and uncertain. Beat: hope with complications; victory isn't tidy.

chapters.title: The Charm Shop Reopens
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys reopens their shop openly, teaching hedge-witchery to anyone who asks. Beat: warmth; invisibility exchanged for community.

chapters.title: What Was Given Away
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable shows Emrys journals documenting everything they sacrificed, letting them choose what to reclaim from record. Beat: memory as gift others can hold for you.

chapters.title: Winter's End
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Spring's first thaw; the Brambles recover; Marrow visits; Pip graduates to journeywoman witch. Beat: fullness—the found family gathered and growing.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Realms send envoys to sign the renewed covenant at the Stones, Emrys presiding. Beat: institutional healing mirroring personal healing.

chapters.title: The Taste of Bread
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Sable bakes Emrys's mother's recipe from the journals; Emrys tastes it as if for the first time and weeps without knowing why. Beat: elegy and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: Garden and Veil Anew
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, closing. Planting a garden behind the shop beneath newly returned stars, Emrys reflects that some things, once given, root deeper than memory. Beat: peace earned; the door left open for wonder.
